# What the privacy boundary costs in accuracy

**Corpus:** 20 documents, 20 pages. Model: `local/qwen2.5:7b`, on this machine over loopback, both arms.

| Arm | Leak rate | Over-redaction | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|
| typed placeholders (what the tool does) | 30.1% (21.7% to 39.0%), n=133 | 19.0% (15.4% to 22.8%), n=379 | 30.5% (26.1% to 34.9%), n=512 |
| raw text (what the tool refuses to do) | 60.2% (53.7% to 66.7%), n=133 | 7.4% (5.2% to 9.7%), n=379 | 14.1% (11.1% to 17.5%), n=512 |

The two arms gave the same category on **55.7%** of the 244 spans both were asked about.

Both arms run on the same local model because the raw arm sends names and this repository's rule is that names do not leave the machine; see the module docstring in `sever/eval/placeholders.py`. That makes the comparison exact and makes the size of the effect a statement about a small open-weights model rather than about the frontier model the pipeline uses. The shape of the effect is what this measures.
